record.paper_title: Recent advances and open questions on the susy structure of the chiral de Rham Complex
record.context_brief: N=1 superconformal algebra generated by global G±
record.original_question: Whenever the local sections G+ and G− given by the curved formula with metric and Christoffel-symbol correction terms glue to global sections of the smooth chiral de Rham complex Ω_ch(M), do they generate two commuting copies of the N=1 superconformal algebra with central charge c = (3/2) dim_R M?

evidence.quote: 4.5 Question. In case G± given by (4.2.1) are globally defined sections of ΩchM, do they generate two commuting copies of the N = 1 superconformal algebra of central charge c = 3/2 dimR M?

The second question is now simply a local computation so it is a matter of computing OPEs in a free field theory of two vectors explicitly given and there exists well established software packages to assist.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold of real dimension $d=\dim_{\mathbb R} M$, and let $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}(M)$ denote the smooth chiral de Rham complex of $M$, viewed as a sheaf of topological vertex superalgebras on $M$. On a coordinate chart with local coordinates $(x^i)$, bosonic fields $b_i, a^i$ and fermionic fields $\varphi^i,\psi_i$, define the local sections
$$G^{\pm} \;=\; g^{ij}\,\psi_i\,\partial b_j \;\pm\; \tfrac{1}{2}\,\Gamma^{i}_{jk}\,\psi_i\,\varphi^{j}\,a^{k} \;+\; (\text{prescribed metric/Christoffel correction terms}),$$
constructed from the Riemannian metric $g$ and its Levi-Civita Christoffel symbols $\Gamma^{i}_{jk}$ in the standard way, such that their sum and difference correspond to the de Rham differential and codifferential on $M$.

Question: Suppose that on a given Riemannian manifold $M$ the locally defined sections $G^{+}$ and $G^{-}$ above patch together to define global sections of $\Omega^{\mathrm{ch}}(M)$. Do $G^{+}$ and $G^{-}$ then generate, inside the vertex algebra of global sections, two mutually commuting copies of the $N=1$ Neveu–Schwarz (super-Virasoro) vertex algebra, each of central charge
$$c \;=\; \tfrac{3}{2}\,\dim_{\mathbb R} M\,?$$
artifact.category_tag: chiral de Rham complex / vertex superalgebras
artifact.status_search_result: The local computation that the curved $G^\pm$ generate two commuting copies of the $N=1$ Neveu–Schwarz algebra of central charge $\tfrac{3}{2}\dim_{\mathbb R} M$ is established in the literature on the chiral de Rham complex on Riemannian manifolds (Ekstrand–Heluani–Källén–Zabzine, and Heluani–Zabzine), with extensions to $N=2$ and $N=4$ in Kähler/Calabi–Yau/hyperkähler cases. The remaining global-existence/gluing issue for $G^\pm$ is what makes the question conditional; once globality is assumed the algebraic statement reduces to a verifiable OPE computation, and the relevant pieces appear in the cited works, but a single explicit reference fully asserting the conditional statement on a general Riemannian manifold is not clearly identified, so it is best regarded as partially settled.

status_evidence.title: Chiral de Rham complex on Riemannian manifolds and special holonomy
status_evidence.snippet: On a Riemannian manifold the chiral de Rham complex carries an N=1 superconformal structure; in Calabi–Yau and hyperkähler cases one obtains two commuting copies with half central charge.
status_evidence.claim: Two commuting copies of supersymmetry algebras arise from the CDR in special holonomy cases.

status_evidence.title: Supersymmetry of the Chiral de Rham Complex
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of N=1 (and extended) superconformal structures on the chiral de Rham complex of a Riemannian manifold.
status_evidence.claim: The N=1 superconformal structure on CDR is constructed from metric and Christoffel data.

status_evidence.title: The global sections of the chiral de Rham complex on a Kummer surface
status_evidence.snippet: Studies global sections of CDR and the resulting extended superconformal algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Global gluing of the supersymmetry currents underlies the algebra of global sections.
